t: A Hunkpapa Lakota named Jumping Badger at birth, he took his father's name, Tȟatȟáŋka Íyotake, after counting coup on a Crow warrior at 14, and as a man refused any dependence on the United States government.
In 1876 he gathered a large camp of Lakota and Northern Cheyenne, performed the Sun Dance and had a vision of soldiers falling; the camp defeated the 7th Cavalry under Custer on 25 June 1876.

After four years in Canada he surrendered in 1881, toured with Buffalo Bill's Wild West, and was killed on 15 December 1890 by agency police who were sent to arrest him because officials feared he would join the Ghost Dance.
dyk: After the Sun Dance of 1876, Sitting Bull described a vision of soldiers, "as thick as grasshoppers", falling upside down into the Lakota camp; about three weeks later the camp defeated Custer's 7th Cavalry.
ev: Born as Ȟoká Psíče (Jumping Badger), a Hunkpapa Lakota, sometime between 1831 and 1837
He is among the leaders of the defenders of a village attacked by two brigades under Brigadier General Alfred Sully, and is shot in the hip in September
Gall and other Hunkpapa sign the Treaty of Fort Laramie; Sitting Bull does not agree to it
The Lakota and Northern Cheyenne defeat Custer's 7th Cavalry at the Little Bighorn on 25 June
He leads his band across the border to Wood Mountain in the North-West Territories
Hunger forces him and 186 followers to return and surrender at Fort Buford on 19 July
He leaves the reservation to appear with Buffalo Bill's Wild West for four months
Agency police try to arrest him on 15 December; he is shot dead

f.born: Between 1831 and 1837, on land later included in the Dakota Territory; a great-grandson asserted in 2007, from family oral tradition, that it was along the Yellowstone River south of present-day Miles City, Montana; named Ȟoká Psíče (Jumping Badger) at birth; Hunkpapa Lakota
f.died: 15 December 1890 at his house on the Standing Rock Reservation, shot in the chest and head by Standing Rock policemen Lieutenant Bull Head and Red Tomahawk during an attempt to arrest him
f.role: Hunkpapa Lakota leader and spiritual leader who led his people in resistance to United States government policies; the ostensible head of the Lakota coalition of 1876
f.known: resistance to the Northern Pacific Railway survey; refusal to sign or sell under the 1868 Treaty of Fort Laramie; the Sun Dance vision before the Little Bighorn; exile in Canada (1877–1881); surrender in 1881; the Wild West show of 1885; his death during the arrest of 1890
